learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic concepts of molecular biology, as well as the properties and peculiarities of biomedical data from mass sequencing technologies.
Understand the principle of sequence alignment and the different algorithms that implement it.
Apply the most common tools and algorithms to process data in the context of molecular biology.
Use the most appropriate machine learning paradigms to extract the maximum amount of information from the data.
Build predictive or descriptive models to characterize samples of biomedical interest.
Interpret the results in the context from which the data originates.
Effectively communicate the results obtained through machine learning.

syllabus_topics: Basic Concepts of Molecular Biology. The flow of genetic information. Fundamentals of molecular evolution.
Biological Databases. Searches focused on genes, variants, mutations and biological information. Predictions from biological sequences.
Genomic Technologies. DNA and RNA sequencing. Detection of epigenetic modifications.
Sequence analysis and alignment. Sequence and alignment formats and tools.
Detection of mutations and SNP genotyping. Filtering of variants and mutations. Techniques for validating variants and mutations.
Arrays and genomic expression. Formats and tools.
Association studies. Population and statistical concepts. Mendelian randomization.
Practices: Obtaining biological information from public databases.
Practices: Processing genomic and transcriptomic data.
Practices: Integration of biological information and visualization of results.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as: 0.1 x APC + 0.1 x CV + 0.4 x TP + 0.4 x ET. No minimum grades are established for any section. For the extraordinary call, the evaluable elements are TP (with presentation and defense) and ET. Students who scored 5 or more in ET or TP during the ordinary call can retake only the failed part. The final grade for the extraordinary call is calculated as: 0.5 x TP + 0.5 x ET. Students with differentiated evaluation will be assessed in the same way as in extraordinary calls.
